item.title: Reddit Fights Teen Account Ban: Platforms contest Australia’s under-16 law; ruling may sway global curbs
item.description: In late 2025, Australia enacted a law prohibiting individuals under 16 from accessing social media. However, Reddit and a libertarian organization are contesting this legislation in the High Court. While the law seeks to safeguard youth, it faces backlash for its lacking effectiveness, as many teenagers under this age still manage to go online. The government has responded by imposing stricter penalties on non-compliant social media platforms.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Wisconsin father-son dealership feud ends with $321,330 civil-theft damages against son
item.description: A serious conflict arose between Carl Schneider and his son Chris regarding Hybrid Car Store Inc., their family-run dealership. Chris misappropriated corporate funds to pay off personal obligations, resulting in significant financial repercussions. The situation escalated with multiple lawsuits, resulting in a federal court ruling that held Chris accountable for civil theft.

item.title: Record 2026 Campaign Spending: Billionaires, crypto fuel $11.9bn US midterms; TV ads dominate
item.description: The 2026 midterm elections in the U.S. are on track to raise a staggering $12 billion, marking the most expensive campaign in history. Wealthy individuals and corporations wield increasing influence over financing, with billionaire Elon Musk standing out as the top donor, having contributed nearly $500 million to Republican candidates.

item.title: Netanyahu open to 'broad' government formation after election setback but rules out Arab parties
item.description: Benjamin Netanyahu has expressed a readiness to establish a broad coalition government under his guidance. His Likud party is attempting to stall the certification process of the recent election results, citing claims of foreign interference. Netanyahu has dismissed the option of collaborating with Arab parties, due to accusations of terrorism against them.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: 26 killed as Russia strikes Ukraine school used for aid distribution
item.description: Russian forces struck a school being used as a humanitarian aid distribution centre in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, killing at least 26 people, with around 20 others missing. Rescue efforts were disrupted by fresh drone attacks. Meanwhile, cyberattacks triggered fake emergency alerts in Ukraine and Russia, as a limited ceasefire in the Kherson region expired.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Mishra

item.title: Judge Clears Capitol Event: US court backs Satanic Temple’s free speech claim; Iowa plans appeal
item.description: In a significant ruling, a federal judge has mandated that Iowa officials allow the local chapter of the Satanic Temple to hold its holiday event. This decision comes after multiple rejections linked to building regulations. Despite state officials' reservations about the event, the judge found their concerns unconvincing. Activities scheduled include caroling and crafts for children. However, state officials are prepared to contest the ruling's validity.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Atlanta landlord's $50,000 fundraiser grows into $16.5 million, helping 5,500 families avoid eviction
item.description: Jason Dozier initiated a fundraising campaign in 2020, which led to the creation of the Housing Stability Fund. This programme has provided financial assistance to over 5,500 families facing housing insecurity in the Atlanta area. By streamlining processes and collaborating with landlords, the programme aims to prevent evictions and court backlogs. Follow-up surveys indicate that a majority of recipients remain in stable housing a year later.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Howard Stern's wife Beth turns grief into rescue mission, helping over 2,000 cats find homes
item.description: After the heartbreaking passing of their bulldog, Howard and Beth Stern channeled their sorrow into meaningful change by founding Bianca's Furry Friends Feline Adoption Center, part of North Shore Animal League America. This center improves the conditions for cats waiting for adoption and boosts rescue capabilities. With over 2,000 cats fostered since 2013, Beth's dedicated efforts have played a crucial role in spotlighting the importance of adopting shelter animals nationwide.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Stephen Curry-backed golf teams make history with women's first NEC title and men's third win
item.description: Howard University's golf program reached new heights when both men's and women's teams won their conference championships. The women's team claimed its first-ever Northeast Conference title in April 2026. Just days later, the men's team secured its third consecutive NEC championship victory. The successes highlighted the growth of the program, supported by NBA star Stephen Curry's funding.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Maryland court orders new trial over $3.2 million trust after sisters challenge inheritance
item.description: A Maryland appeals court has mandated a new trial concerning a $3.2 million trust fund held by three sisters. The court identified procedural errors that prevented two sisters from presenting crucial handwriting evidence regarding the trust. Their claims included accusations of undue influence exerted by their sister, the main beneficiary. The appeals court emphasized issues with the previous trial's allowed testimonies and evidence exclusions.

item.title: Mammal Reintroductions At Sturt: six native species return; project expands beyond fences
item.description: Ecologists Rebecca West and Reece Pedler are leading an inspiring initiative called the Wild Deserts project in New South Wales, focused on reviving native mammal populations that have been absent for over a century. Their efforts have successfully seen the reintroduction of multiple species to Sturt National Park, where they are now thriving and breeding in the wild.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Murtho Habitat Restoration: Former vineyard revived for regent parrots; family project spans generations
item.description: After departing from the wine industry, Tony and Cherie Townsend embarked on a remarkable project to repurpose their 40-acre vineyard into a sanctuary for regent parrots. Their family and local volunteers, spanning four generations, are actively involved in this conservation initiative. Backed by the Murraylands and Riverland Landscape Board, over 3,000 native seedlings have been planted, fostering vital habitats and illustrating the crucial role private land plays in enhancing biodiversity.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Nebraska court vacates sale of couple's home over husband's commercial lease debt
item.description: A couple in Nebraska was on the brink of losing their family home due to a commercial lease debt solely tied to the husband. The creditor aimed to sell the property to reclaim funds. The Nebraska Supreme Court stepped in, clarifying that the lower court misapplied the judgment lien, which only affected the husband's interest.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Record Subsurface Warming In Monterey Bay: MBARI logs 18.18°C at 60m; tropical species move north
item.description: Scientists have announced that temperatures at 200 feet off Monterey Bay have reached their highest levels in nearly forty years. This rise is attributed to the forthcoming 2026-27 El Niño, with sightings of tropical species migrating northward, suggesting significant ecological transformations. These shifts in ocean conditions pose a risk to deep-sea food availability, impacting various marine ecosystems.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk
